title: Three 2027 renewals on one London street

hook.spoken: Three neighbours on one London street renew in 2027. Same mortgage. Only one of them gets the payment jump.

alts.text: Will your 2027 renewal cost more? One date decides it, and it isn't renewal day.
+$402 or -$200 a month. Same $500K mortgage, same 2027 renewal year.

angle: Every competitor tells 2027 renewers to brace for payment shock. Bank of Canada data says that only holds for people who signed before rates climbed. On one illustrative London street, three neighbours with the same $500,000 mortgage renew in 2027: the Feb 2022 signer pays about $402 more a month, while the Nov 2022 and Mar 2024 signers pay less at today's average rate. The viewer guesses which one before the reveal, then learns the two moves that matter for both groups, including the lender switch (Dan's renewals and transfers service) that no longer needs a new stress test.

Service: 'Mortgage Renewal/ Transferring your mortgage' (the straight-switch slide is a transfer)

styleWhy: This is a data story told against the received news ('renewal shock'), so the Front Page lets the reveal land as a correction on the record, with each neighbour's payment run as the graphic in place of a news photo and 'Continued on slide N' doing the swiping.
device: A fictional front page, 'The 2027 Renewal Report', dateline London, Ont.: three neighbours A, B and C sit as three columns on the front page with their signing date and rate; the guess is set on slide 2; the inner pages are one graphic page per neighbour (halftone bars from $0: payment then vs payment at renewal, spot colour on the new payment).
structure: Carousel 9: hook, second hook (pick one), three reveals, why, what to do if you pay less, save-worthy recap, one send CTA. Guess-then-reveal runs from slide 2 to slide 5.

mechanic.how: Slide 2 lists the three neighbours (A: Feb 2022 at 2.81%, B: Nov 2022 at 5.17%, C: Mar 2024 3-year at 5.43%) and says 'Pick the one whose payment jumps, then swipe.' Slides 3-5 reveal them one by one, so the viewer has to swipe to check their guess. Most people pick wrong, because they expect all three to go up.

title: The 20%-down trap: London's 2022 buyers

hook.spoken: Bought in London in early 2022 with 20% down? At your 2027 renewal you may have fewer lenders to choose from than the buyer who put less down.
hook.pattern: Who the rule catches (short sweeping claim viewers want to check; LESSONS 2026-11-17/19)

alts.text: $825,221 then. $601,289 now. London's average price, and the start of your 2027 renewal.
20% down felt like the safe move in 2022. At a 2027 renewal, the buyer with less down can have more lenders to pick from.

angle: London had one of Ontario's sharpest peak-to-now drops: the LSTAR average was $825,221 in Feb 2022 and $601,289 in Oct 2026, about 27% lower. A buyer who put exactly 20% down near the peak has an uninsured mortgage, and a new lender usually won't take an uninsured loan above 80% of today's value. In the illustrative example the loan is 93.5% of value at the Feb 2027 renewal. The twist people want to check: the neighbour who put the minimum down has an insured mortgage, which can usually still move. This is about which lenders can bid on a 2027 renewal, and Dan's renewals and transfers work lives there.

title: Departures: London's 2027 renewal board

hook.main: Renewing by mid-March? Your window's open.
hook.spoken: If your mortgage renews by mid-March 2027, your shopping window is already open. Find your month on the board.

alts.text: Waiting for the renewal letter gives you 21 days. Most lenders would have held a rate for 120.
Renewing in 2027? Find your month on this board before Dec 9.

angle: The landscape scan says nobody is running a renewal countdown. This turns the dates into a London/Komoka departure board: each 2027 renewal month shows when the 120-day rate-hold window opens, when the 21-day renewal letter has to arrive (the 'final call'), and a live status column. As of Nov 19, Jan to mid-March renewers are already inside their window, April opens Dec 2, and the Dec 9 Bank of Canada decision lands inside the window for January to April renewers. It is a lookup tool: you find your row, you act, you send it to the person on the mortgage with you.

Service: 'Mortgage Renewal/ Transferring your mortgage' (slide 8: switching with the same balance needs no new stress test)
Province: Ontario (compliance line above the footer)
format: carousel (feed 1080x1350, 9 slides; board area above the kit footer band)
style: split-flap departure board (one-off, built in custom-html)
styleWhy: This story is a timetable people search for their own row in, and only a departure board makes 'window open / final call' readable at a glance, with one continuous board running across the slide edges, which neither broadsheet nor paper-trail can build.
device: A code-drawn split-flap board (charcoal housing, off-white flap tiles with a hairline split, every character live type in a mono face such as IBM Plex Mono or Geist Mono). Header 'LONDON · KOMOKA  |  RENEWALS 2027'. Columns: RENEWS · WINDOW OPENS · FINAL CALL · STATUS. Status lamps use Dan's sky blue (#13AFF0) for OPEN NOW, flat with no glow; navy (#002E6E) housing accents. Rows on slides 3-5 are one continuous board, cut across the slide seams so a row visibly continues into the next slide.
structure: Carousel 9: hook board, second hook (120 vs 21), three board panels (Jan-Apr, May-Aug, Sep-Dec), what a hold does, why now (Dec 9), save-worthy recap, send CTA.

mechanic.type: find-your-row lookup with a countdown status column, plus a swipe cue that crosses the slide edge
mechanic.how: The cover ends with a board row cut by the right edge and an arrow ('Find your month ▸'). Slides 3-5 are one board split across three slides; the STATUS column counts down ('OPEN NOW', 'OPENS DEC 2', 'OPENS IN 43 DAYS') from the post date, computed in build.mjs. People swipe until they find their month, then send it to their co-borrower.

risks: 120 days is common lender practice, not a rule (bank-direct holds are often 90 days). Keep 'most lenders' and 'up to', and the fine line on slide 5.
The 21-day statement rule applies to federally regulated lenders; credit unions follow provincial rules. Fine print says so.
Statuses are date-dependent: build.mjs computes them from the scheduled post date; if the post slips, re-render.

Agency echo: the brian-wang 'portfolio-failing' reel (Nov 17, news-package) used split-flap boards. Different client and format, but the critic should make sure this board has its own look (housing colour, type, column logic).
Same-week overlap: the nightly plan gives Dan a face reel 'Renewal letter in hand: three checks' whose check 2 is the 120-day hold. If both run, space them a week apart or change that check.
build: custom-html from bin/custom_html_skeleton.mjs: footer band and verbatim complianceLine on every slide, safe-box check above the footer top. Board tiles are HTML/CSS (no canvas text). Body type >= 28 px: 4 columns x 4 rows per panel fits at about 34-40 px mono; drop the year from dates to keep width. Procedural grain only, no gradients or glow on lamps. About 1-3 h build.
